# Volume 3 — Chapter IV April’s Lady

!!! note "Source text"
    Passages cited on the wiki pages link into this page. Only volumes at or before
    this page's cutoff are present.

Portmaris is a charming old town, recalling early Colonial times, and enveloped in its antique ambiance, like a refined old lady wearing clothes made after the style of her younger years. In places it shoots forth into modern times, yet down deep it remains uncorrupted; it abounds in strange relics, and is encircled by the romance of numerous tales from bygone days. At one time it was simply a frontier post on the border of the wild country, and during those times Indians prevented existence from becoming dull for the inhabitants. Afterwards it developed into a source of conflict between the British and the French, being held at times by the former and at times by the latter, coming out of every possession with a new mark of fighting countries stamped upon it.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0000 }

Within its park stands a martello tower covered with the signatures of visitors, a decommissioned former French fortification occupies the hills outside the municipality, and a few old-fashioned cannons sit in its public plazas. It contains additional historical sites as well, which inquisitive people can discover, and not one is as charming and appealing as Old St. John’s Cemetery situated in the absolute center of the community, bordered by avenues of peaceful, historic residences on two flanks, and active, energetic, contemporary avenues on the remaining ones. Each inhabitant of Portmaris experiences a surge of personal pride regarding Old St. John’s, because, should he possess any status whatsoever, he possesses a forefather interred within it, having an odd, tilted stone placed at his crown, or otherwise lying flat defensively across the plot, upon which every primary detail of his life is documented. Generally, no significant artistry or craftsmanship was expended upon those ancient markers. The majority consist of coarsely carved native brown or gray stone, and a desire for decoration is present in merely a handful of instances. A few are decorated with a skull and cross-bones, and this macabre motif is often paired with the face of a cherub. Numerous stones are fallen and broken. The passage of time has eroded nearly every one, to the point where certain epitaphs are entirely erased, while others are barely readable with effort. The burial ground is extremely crowded and densely shaded, as it is encircled and crossed by lines of elms and willows, under whose canopy the rested ought to sleep without dreams, continuously lulled by the breezes and foliage above them, and entirely untroubled by the noise of vehicles immediately outside.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0001 }

The following afternoon, Nell embarked on the first of numerous walks through Old St. John’s. Earlier, during the morning, she and Honora had traveled to Wexcombe to enroll as students, an errand that left them with no further duties for the remainder of the day. Being encircled by throngs of unfamiliar people—the majority of whom seemed somewhat out of place, as though uncertain of their proper standing—was far from uplifting, so the girls were pleased to make their departure.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0002 }

Small, separate clusters of two or three “freshettes” were standing around, eyeing one another suspiciously; more astute in their time and era, the “freshies” had formed a single group on the main hallway’s large staircase, from which they were beltly singing glees with all the energy of young lungs to challenge their customary foes, the Sophomores, several of whom were roaming around in a superior manner, appearing suitably contemptuous of the “unlicked cubs” occupying the steps. Hugh and Wilfred could not be spotted anywhere.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0003 }

“Rarely had it occurred to me that I would one day rejoice at seeing a Mott,” stated Honora while they walked across the campus, “yet I would receive Wilfred’s bulging eyes with near ecstasy. They would, if nothing else, be eyes I recognize.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0004 }

“Oh,” Nell sighed. “I am unable to put into words my emotions while I stood in that place, awaiting my turn for registration—feeling as unimportant as the smallest droplet inside a huge bucket. Feeling unimportant is awful enough, but having it forced deep into your spirit that you shall not ever, can not ever, become anything other than unimportant is intolerable, and that represents my exact feelings—like I was unseeable by the unaided eye and a few of those Sophs could crush me underfoot. I was certain that I’d enter my tomb without tears, honor, or song.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0005 }

“Just hold out until next year,” Honora offered consolingly. “At that point, we can appear just as unimpressed and worldly as any single Sophomore among them. Feeling unimportant is certainly quite unpleasant; however, I believe it surpasses feeling as huge and clumsy as I felt—like I was stretched out across the entirety of Wexcombe. I experienced that feeling—presumably since I exceeded everyone else in the gathering by a solid two inches in height. My fear wasn't that a Soph would step on me; my fear was that they would mistake me for an elephant, or a excessively large instance of a potato-nourished Islander.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0006 }

“I imagine our difficulty lies in our inability to pardon large Wexcombe for failing to be small Regent’s,” Nell stated, drawing her former sunny outlook around herself to clothe her inner desolation. “On our departure from Regent’s, we were acquainted with all the locals and occupied a position unique to us. It seems we were unwittingly anticipating that we would resume existence at Wexcombe at the exact point we ceased at Regent’s, leaving us currently feeling disoriented. It is a relief that my current mental condition is unknown to Mrs. Sowerby and Mrs. Elisha Duckett, and that they will remain ignorant of it forever. They would take delight in declaring ‘I told you so,’ believing it signaled the start of the conclusion. In truth, it merely marks the conclusion of the start.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0007 }

“Precisely. That seems more Anneish. Soon enough we will be acclimated and acquainted, and everything will be fine. Nell, did you see the girl who spent the whole morning standing by herself right outside the coeds’ dressing room door—the attractive one possessing brown eyes and a crooked mouth?”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0008 }

“Indeed, I noticed. She stood out to me especially as she appeared to be the sole being present who appeared just as isolated and without companions as I felt inside. Though I possessed you, she was entirely on her own.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0009 }

“I believe she experienced a strong sense of isolation, as well. On a few occasions I noticed her start to move in our direction, yet she failed to carry it through—owing to shyness, most likely. It was my desire that she join us. Had I not experienced such a strong resemblance to the previously mentioned pachyderm, I would have approached her myself. However, I lacked the ability to clamber across that vast room while every one of those young men was shouting from the staircase. Among the new female students I observed throughout the day, she possessed the greatest beauty, though it is likely that grace proves deceptive and fairness itself counts for nothing during one's initial day at Wexcombe,” Honora said in closing, accompanied by laughter.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0010 }

“I’m heading over to Old St. John’s following lunch,” Nell stated. “A cemetery might not be an ideal location for lifting one's spirits, yet it appears to be the sole accessible spot possessing trees, and I simply cannot do without trees. I intend to take a seat on an old slab, close my eyes, and pretend that I am situated within the Brierley woods.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0011 }

Instead of doing so, Nell discovered plenty to captivate her in Old St. John’s that kept her eyes fully attentive. Passing through the entrance gates, they moved beyond the unadorned, heavy stone arch capped by England's magnificent lion.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0012 }

“‘And the wild bramble on Inkerman remains bloody, And in history those desolate heights shall from now on be celebrated,’”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0013 }

quoted Nell, eyeing it with a shudder of excitement. A shadowy, chilly, verdant spot enveloped them, a domain where breezes enjoyed humming. Along the extended turf-covered walkways they roamed, deciphering the unusual, lengthy inscriptions, chiseled during an era possessing greater free time than ours.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0014 }

“‘Here lieth the body of Albert Crawford, Esq.,’” Nell recited off a gray, weathered slab, “‘for many years Keeper of His Majesty’s Ordnance at Portmaris. He served in the army till the peace of 1763, when he retired from bad health. He was a brave officer, the best of husbands, the best of fathers, the best of friends. He died October 29th, 1792, aged 84 years.’ That is quite an epitaph, Sukey. It surely offers some ‘scope for imagination.’ What a great deal of adventure a life like that must have contained! As for his character, I do not think human praise could possibly surpass it. I wonder if people informed him of all those finest traits during his lifetime.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0015 }

“Another one is right here,” Honora remarked. “Listen—
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0016 }

“To the memory of Alexander Ross, who passed away at 43 years of age on September 22, 1840. Erected as a token of affection by someone he served with such fidelity for 27 years that he was considered a friend, worthy of complete trust and devotion.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0017 }

“That is a fine inscription for a tomb,” Nell remarked after a moment’s thought. “I could not ask for anything superior. Every person serves in one way or another, and provided the truth of our fidelity can be honestly carved upon our markers, nothing further is required. Sukey, take a look at this sad small slate marker—‘in remembrance of a beloved child.’ Furthermore, another one here states it was ‘built in remembrance of a person interred in another place.’ I am curious about the location of that unfamiliar resting site. In truth, Nonie, modern cemeteries can never match the fascination of this place. Your statement was correct—this location will see me frequently. My affection for it is already established. It appears other people are present—a young woman stands at the far portion of this path.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0018 }

“Indeed, and my thought is that she is the exact young woman who came under our notice at Wexcombe earlier today. My eyes have been fixed on her for five minutes. Precisely six times she has begun to walk up the avenue, and precisely six times she has wheeled around and returned. Her condition is either one of terrible shyness, or her conscience is burdened by something. We should walk out to meet her. My feeling is that making an acquaintance is simpler in a graveyard than it is at Wexcombe.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0019 }

Along the extended grassy arcade, they strolled toward the unknown woman, who sat upon a gray stone beneath a massive willow tree. She was unquestionably quite lovely, possessing a striking, uneven, captivating sort of beauty. Her satiny hair exhibited a luster resembling brown nuts, and her plump cheeks carried a gentle, mature warmth. Beneath curiously angled black eyebrows, her eyes were large, dark, and plush, while her uneven lips were the color of a red rose. She was dressed in a stylish brown suit, from under which a pair of extremely fashionable small shoes poked out; and her dull pink straw headwear, encircled by golden-brown poppies, possessed that subtle, undeniable quality belonging to the “creation” of a master hatter. Honora experienced an abrupt, sharp awareness that her own headpiece was the work of her local shopkeeper, while Nell felt an uneasy doubt about whether the shirt she had sewn herself, which Mrs. Sowerby had adjusted, appeared excessively rustic and rustic-made in comparison to the unknown woman's elegant outfit. During that instant, each girl considered retreating.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0020 }

However, they had currently halted and faced the gray slab. Retracting was impossible now, because the girl with brown eyes had obviously assumed that they intended to talk with her. At once, she leaped to her feet and advanced, extending her hand with a bright, welcoming smile that appeared completely devoid of both timidness and a guilty conscience.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0021 }

“Oh, I am longing to find out who you two girls are,” she cried out enthusiastically. “I have been desperate to discover it. I caught sight of you at Wexcombe earlier today. Tell me, was it not terrible there? Briefly, I found myself wishing I had remained at home and wed.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0022 }

Nell along with Honora both burst into unrestrained laughter upon hearing this unforeseen ending. Laughing as well was the girl with the brown eyes.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0023 }

“I honestly did. I was capable of it, you see. Come along, let us all take a seat on this tombstone and become familiar. It will not be difficult. I am certain we will be fond of one another—I was aware of it the moment I noticed you at Wexcombe earlier today. I had such a strong desire to walk straight across and embrace you two.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0024 }

“Why didn’t you?” Honora inquired.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0025 }

“For the simple reason that I was unable to resolve to act. Personal decisions are something I can never reach on my own—indecisiveness is a constant burden to me. The moment I choose a path, an inner feeling tells me that a different option would have been the right one. Though it is a terrible handicap, it is an innate trait of mine, meaning there is no point in criticizing me over it, as certain individuals are prone to do. Consequently, I was unable to reach a decision to approach and talk with you, despite my strong desire to.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0026 }

“We assumed your shyness was holding you back,” Nell remarked.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0027 }

“No, no, my dear. Shyness is not one of the numerous faults—or good qualities—possessed by Cressida Lindsay—Cressy as a nickname. Please use Cressy for me from the start. Well then, what are your names?”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0028 }

“That one is Honora Hollis,” Nell said while pointing.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0029 }

“And that one is Nell Harcourt,” Honora said, gesturing toward her next.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0030 }

“And we hail from the Island,” the two of them uttered in unison.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0031 }

“Harborough, Nova Scotia, is where I come from,” said Cressida.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0032 }

“Harborough!” cried Nell. “Why, I was born in that place.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0033 }

“Are you actually being serious? Well, that means you are a Bluenose when all is said and done.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0034 }

“No, it doesn’t,” Nell fired back. “Wasn’t Dan O’Connell the one who said that a man being born in a stable didn't turn him into a horse? I’m Island through and through.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0035 }

“Anyway, I am happy that Harborough was your birthplace. It renders us somewhat like neighbors, does it not? I am pleased by that, for I will not feel like I am revealing secrets to an unknown person when I share them with you. Expressing them is something I must do. Keeping secrets is impossible for me—trying to do so is futile. That is my greatest flaw—that one, along with my previously mentioned indecisiveness. Can you imagine?—deciding which hat to put on when I was preparing to come here took me thirty minutes—here, to a cemetery! Initially, my preference was my brown hat featuring the feather; however, the moment it was on my head, I felt this pink hat possessing the floppy brim would prove more flattering. Once I had it secured with pins, the brown hat appealed to me more. Eventually, I positioned the two of them side by side upon the bed, closed my eyes, and thrust a hat pin at them. The pin pierced the pink hat, which led to me wearing it. It suits me, does it not? Express your opinion, how do my looks strike you?”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0036 }

Upon hearing this innocent request, uttered with utter gravity, Honora chuckled once more. Nell, however, spontaneously pressed Cressida's hand and spoke,
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0037 }

“It seemed to us earlier today that you were the most attractive girl we came across in Wexcombe.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0038 }

A captivating, uneven grin showed on Cressida’s asymmetrical mouth, revealing tiny, exceptionally white teeth.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0039 }

“That was my own thought,” she surprisingly declared next, “yet I needed the viewpoint of another person to reinforce my own. Even regarding how I look, I cannot make up my mind. The moment I have concluded that I am attractive, a miserable feeling comes over me that I am not. On top of that, there is a dreadful old great-aunt of mine who constantly tells me, while sighing mournfully, ‘You were such a pretty baby. It’s strange how children change when they grow up.’ Aunts I love, but great-aunts I hate. If it is not a bother, please assure me frequently that I am attractive. Believing that I am attractive makes me feel far more at ease. Furthermore, I will willingly do the same for you if you desire—which I can do with a clean conscience.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0040 }

“Thanks,” Nell laughed, “however Honora and I believe so strongly in our own beauty that we require no reassurance regarding it, so you do not have to bother.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0041 }

“Ah, you are poking fun at me. You believe I am dreadfully conceited, I am aware, yet that is untrue. Truly, not a single trace of conceit exists within me. Furthermore, I am always quite generous with offering praise to different girls if it is earned. Knowing you people brings me such happiness. My arrival was on Saturday, and homesickness has almost killed me ever since. That sensation is dreadful, wouldn't you say? Within Harborough, my status is that of a notable figure, whereas within Portmaris, I am merely a nobody! Certain moments occurred where I imagined my very spirit transforming into a pale shade of blue. What is your dwelling place?”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0042 }

“Thirty-eight St. John’s Street.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0043 }

“Things are improving. Indeed, my location is right nearby on Wallace Street. However, I am not fond of my boardinghouse. The place feels desolate and solitary, and the view from my window shows a truly hideous rear yard. No other spot on earth is as unattractive. Regarding cats—it seems impossible that every cat in Portmaris gathers there after dark, yet fifty percent of them surely do. It delights me when cats lounge on hearth rugs, napping in front of pleasant, welcoming fires, whereas cats in rear yards in the middle of the night transform into completely distinct creatures. During my initial night in this place, I wept throughout the entire night, and those cats wailed just the same. My nose presented a sight the next morning. I longed deeply to have stayed at home!”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0044 }

“If your indecision is truly so great, I am at a loss to understand how you ever brought yourself to travel to Wexcombe,” remarked an entertained Honora.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0045 }

“May God bless your soul, my dear, I was not the one. My presence here was desired by my father instead. He had completely fixed his mind on this outcome—for what reason, I am uncertain. Is it not entirely absurd to imagine myself working toward a Bachelor of Arts degree? That is not to say I am incapable of achieving it, naturally. My intellect is quite abundant.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0046 }

“Oh!” Honora uttered in an absentminded manner.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0047 }

“Indeed. However, employing them requires such strenuous effort. Furthermore, B.A.’s are bound to be such scholarly, stately, sagacious, and serious beings. No, traveling to Wexcombe was not my desire. My sole reason for doing so was to accommodate father. He is truly a darling. Additionally, I recognized that remaining at home would force me into matrimony. Mother desired that—desired it unequivocally. Mother possesses a great deal of firmness. Yet the prospect of marriage for another few years was something I truly detested. I wish to enjoy an abundance of amusement prior to settling down. Moreover, as preposterous as the notion of me holding a B.A. sounds, the notion of me becoming an elderly married woman is even more comical, wouldn’t you say? My age is merely eighteen. No, my decision was that I preferred traveling to Wexcombe over getting married. On top of that, in what way could I have ever decided upon which suitor to wed?”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0048 }

“Was the number truly that large?” Nell chuckled.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0049 }

“Loads. I am liked tremendously by the lads—they truly do like me. However, merely two of them were of any importance. The others lacked both sufficient age and wealth. A wealthy man is a necessity for my marriage, as you are aware.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0050 }

“Why do you have to?”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0051 }

“Darling, you are unable to picture me as the spouse of a destitute man, aren’t you? Not one helpful task can be performed by me, plus I waste vast amounts of money. Ah, negative, my spouse is required to possess mountains of wealth. Thus my choices were reduced to a pair. However, making a choice between a pair was not a bit simpler than selecting among two hundred. It was entirely clear to me that no matter which single one was chosen by me, my entire existence would be filled with remorse that the alternative had not been wedded.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0052 }

“Wasn't either—of them—loved by you?” Nell inquired, somewhat tentatively. Speaking to an unfamiliar person about life's supreme secret and metamorphosis did not come easily to her.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0053 }

“Heavens, no. Loving anyone is impossible for me. I lack that capacity. Furthermore, I have no desire to. In my opinion, falling in love turns a person into a total slave. Additionally, it would grant a man immense power to inflict pain on you. Fear would take hold of me. No, no, Hector and Orlando are a pair of darling boys, and my fondness for the two of them is so great that determining which one I prefer is truly beyond me. There lies the problem. Naturally, Hector possesses the finest looks, and marrying a man who lacked handsome features is something I just couldn't do. His disposition is pleasant as well, and his dark, curly hair is lovely. He borders on being overly flawless—having a flawless husband doesn't appeal to me, I think—someone in whom I could never discover a flaw.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0054 }

“Then why not marry Orlando?” asked Honora gravely.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0055 }

“Imagine being wedded to a name such as Orlando!” Cressy stated mournfully. “Enduring it seems beyond my ability. Nevertheless, his nose possesses a classic shape, and having a reliable nose in our family would bring relief. Mine cannot be trusted. Up to this point, it resembles the Lindsay style, yet my great fear is that it will display Byrne inclinations as time passes. Daily I inspect it with concern to ensure it remains Lindsay. Mother belonged to the Byrnes and features the Byrne nose to the utmost extent. Just hold on until it comes into your view. Splendid noses are my passion. Nell Harcourt, the nose you have is extraordinarily lovely. His nose almost tipped the scales toward Orlando. Still, Orlando! No, making up my mind proved impossible. Had I been able to handle it like the hats—setting the pair up side by side, closing my eyes, and thrusting with a hatpin—the matter would have been simple.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0056 }

“In what manner were Hector and Orlando feeling at the moment you departed?” asked Honora.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0057 }

“Oh, their hope remains. Having informed them that waiting was required until my decision was reached, I found them entirely agreeable to doing so. You see, I am adored by both of them. My plan in the meantime is to enjoy myself thoroughly. At Wexcombe, my expectation is to be surrounded by a multitude of suitors, as my happiness depends on having them, you know. Yet, is it not your opinion that the first-year students are terribly plain? A single truly good-looking guy was all I noticed in their group, and he departed prior to your arrival. Hugh was the name his friend used when speaking to him, as I overheard. That friend possessed eyes that bulged out to here. Must you leave already, girls? Please stay a while longer.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0058 }

“We must, I think,” Nell remarked, somewhat icily. “The hour is growing late, and I have certain tasks to attend to.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0059 }

“However, the two of you will visit me, isn’t that right?” inquired Cressida, standing up while placing an arm around both of them. “And allow me to visit you. I wish to be friendly with you. I have become so fond of you two. Furthermore, my silliness hasn’t completely repulsed you, has it?”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0060 }

“Not quite,” Nell laughed, answering the squeeze from Cressy with a renewed warmth.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0061 }

“Since I am far less foolish than I appear on the outside, you see. If you merely take Cressida Lindsay as God created her, despite her shortcomings, I think you will grow fond of her in time. Is not this cemetery a charming spot? Being laid to rest here would be wonderful to me. I missed this tomb earlier—the one inside the iron enclosure—oh, girls, come see—the marker states it contains a midshipman who died during the battle between the Shannon and the Chesapeake. Imagine that!”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0062 }

Stopping beside the balustrade, Nell gazed upon the eroded masonry, her blood surging with abrupt exhilaration. The ancient burial ground, featuring its canopy of foliage and extended corridors of shade, dissolved before her eyes. In its place, she envisioned Portmaris Harbor as it appeared almost one hundred years prior. Emerging gradually from the fog was a grand warship, resplendent with “the meteor flag of England.” Following her came a second vessel, carrying on its quarterdeck a motionless, noble figure enfolded in his own star-adorned banner—the brave Lawrence. The hand of Time had reversed its leaf, revealing the Shannon navigating victoriously into the inlet carrying the Chesapeake as her trophy.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0063 }

“Return to us, Nell Harcourt—return,” Cressida giggled, tugging at her sleeve. “A century separates you from us. Return.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0064 }

Nell returned, letting out a sigh, while a soft shine gleamed in her eyes.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0065 }

“That ancient tale has always been a favorite of mine,” she remarked, “and even though the English emerged victorious, my affection for it stems from the valiant, vanquished commander. It feels so close and vividly genuine beside this tomb. Just eighteen years old was this unfortunate young midshipman. His inscription states that he ‘died of desperate wounds received in gallant action.’ A warrior could ask for nothing better.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0066 }

Prior to turning around, Nell unfastened the small bundle of violet pansies pinned to her and let it fall gently onto the burial site of the youth who had died during the massive naval battle.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0067 }

“Well, how do you regard our latest acquaintance?” Honora inquired, once Cressy had departed from their presence.
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0068 }

“She appeals to me. Despite every bit of her foolishness, she possesses a truly endearing quality. I think she speaks the truth when she claims she is not nearly as foolish as she appears. She is a sweet, kissable child—and whether she will ever truly mature remains uncertain to me.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0069 }

“I am fond of her as well,” Honora stated firmly. “Her conversation involves boys just as frequently as Opal Pettigrew’s does. However, listening to Opal constantly makes me furious or disgusted, while Cressy simply made me want to indulge in a kindly laugh. Now, what is the reason for that difference?”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0070 }

“There is a distinction,” Nell remarked thoughtfully. “In my view, it stems from Opal being truly so aware of males. She merely pretends at romance and courting. Furthermore, whenever she brags about her suitors, one gets the impression that her motive is to thoroughly impress upon you that your own fall far short in number. On the other hand, whenever Cressy discusses her suitors, her tone suggests she is merely referring to friends. She genuinely regards males as fine companions, and having scores of them following her around brings her joy solely because she enjoys being well-liked and perceived as well-liked. Even Alex and Orlando—after this, I shall be incapable of considering those two names apart—represent nothing more to her than a pair of companions eager for her to join in their games forever. Meeting her brings me happiness, as does our trip to Old St. John’s. This afternoon, I trust I have extended a small soul-root into the earth of Portmaris. It is my desire, at least. Being transplanted is something I detest.”
{: #nw-v03-c04-p0071 }
